reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical design - Part 2: Ground investigation and testing

sections.title: Scope
sections.summary: EN 1997-2 supplements EN 1997-1, giving rules for planning and reporting of ground investigations, general requirements for commonly used laboratory and field tests, interpretation and evaluation of test results, and derivation of geotechnical parameter values, including worked examples of applying field test results to design.
sections.body: EN 1997 is intended to be used with EN 1990:2002 (basis of structural design) and applies to the geotechnical aspects of the design of buildings and civil engineering works. EN 1997-2 provides rules supplementary to EN 1997-1 related to: planning and reporting of ground investigations; general requirements for a number of commonly used laboratory and field tests; interpretation and evaluation of test results; and derivation of values of geotechnical parameters and coefficients. Examples of the application of field test results to design are given. Establishment of characteristic values is covered in EN 1997-1, not here. This document gives no specific provisions for environmental ground investigations. Only commonly used geotechnical laboratory and field tests are covered, selected on the basis of their importance in geotechnical practice, availability in commercial geotechnical laboratories, and existence of an accepted European testing procedure; laboratory tests on soils are mainly applicable to saturated soils. The provisions apply primarily to geotechnical category 2 projects (EN 1997-1, 2.1); category 1 investigation requirements are normally limited and based on local experience, while category 3 projects normally require at least the category 2 investigation extent plus additional investigations and more advanced tests related to the circumstances placing the project in category 3. The derivation of parameter values is dedicated primarily to the design of pile and spread foundations based on field testing, as detailed in Annexes D, E, F and G of EN 1997-1:2004.
key_points: EN 1997-2 supplements EN 1997-1: planning/reporting of ground investigations, test requirements, interpretation of results, derivation of parameter values
Establishment of characteristic values is covered in EN 1997-1, not EN 1997-2
No specific provisions for environmental ground investigations
Only commonly used, European-standardized laboratory and field tests are covered; lab tests on soils apply mainly to saturated soils
Provisions apply primarily to geotechnical category 2; category 3 needs at least category 2 extent plus additional advanced tests
Parameter derivation is dedicated primarily to pile and spread foundation design from field testing (EN 1997-1 Annexes D, E, F, G)
EN 1997 does not cover special requirements of seismic design (see EN 1998)
sections.applicability: Defines the scope, purpose, and boundary of EN 1997-2 relative to EN 1997-1 for all ground investigation and testing work.

sections.title: Normative references
sections.summary: Lists the normative documents referenced by EN 1997-2: EN 1990, EN 1997-1, the EN ISO 14688/14689 soil and rock identification/classification series, and the EN ISO 22475 (sampling) and EN ISO 22476 (field testing, Parts 1-13: CPT, dynamic probing, SPT, pressuremeters, dilatometers, field vane, plate load) series.
sections.body: The normative references constitute provisions of EN 1997-2 through citation in the text. For dated references, subsequent amendments do not apply; for undated references, the latest edition applies. Key references: EN 1990:2002 (basis of structural design); EN 1997-1:2004 (Eurocode 7 Part 1: General rules); EN ISO 14688-1/-2 (soil identification/classification, description and classification principles); EN ISO 14689-1 (rock identification and description); EN ISO 22475-1 (sampling by drilling and excavation, groundwater measurements - technical principles of execution); and the EN ISO 22476 field-testing series: Part 1 electrical cone/piezocone penetration tests, Part 2 dynamic probing, Part 3 standard penetration test, Part 4 Menard pressuremeter test, Part 5 flexible dilatometer test, Part 6 self-boring pressuremeter test, Part 7 borehole jack test, Part 8 full displacement pressuremeter test, Part 9 field vane test, Part 12 mechanical CPT, and Part 13 plate loading test. A bibliography of CEN ISO Technical Specifications giving further procedural information (e.g. for the weight sounding test and flat dilatometer test) is presented in Annex X.
key_points: EN 1990:2002 and EN 1997-1:2004 are the foundational normative references
EN ISO 14688-1/-2: soil identification, description and classification
EN ISO 14689-1: rock identification and description
EN ISO 22475-1: sampling by drilling/excavation and groundwater measurements

EN ISO 22476 series (Parts 1-13) covers CPT/CPTU, dynamic probing, SPT, pressuremeters (Menard/self-boring/full-displacement), flexible dilatometer, borehole jack, field vane, mechanical CPT, and plate loading tests
CEN ISO/TS technical specifications (weight sounding, flat dilatometer) are listed in the Bibliography (Annex X)
sections.applicability: Identifies the companion standards that EN 1997-2 relies on for execution procedures of each sampling and test method.

sections.title: Assumptions
sections.summary: EN 1997-2 assumes that data required for design are collected, recorded and interpreted by appropriately qualified personnel; that structures are designed by appropriately qualified and experienced personnel; and that adequate continuity and communication exist between data-collection, design, and construction personnel.
sections.body: Reference is made to EN 1990:2002, 1.3 and EN 1997-1:2004, 1.3 for the general Eurocode assumptions. In addition, EN 1997-2 is based on the assumptions that: data required for design are collected, recorded and interpreted by appropriately qualified personnel; structures are designed by appropriately qualified and experienced personnel; and adequate continuity and communication exist between the personnel involved in data-collection, design and construction.
key_points: Data collection, recording, and interpretation must be done by appropriately qualified personnel
Structures must be designed by appropriately qualified and experienced personnel
Continuity and communication between data-collection, design, and construction personnel is assumed
sections.applicability: General personnel-competence and process-continuity assumptions underlying the validity of EN 1997-2's provisions.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.summary: Defines terms specific to EN 1997-2: derived value, disturbed/undisturbed/remoulded sample, measured value, natural/reconstituted/re-compacted/re-consolidated specimen, quality class (5 classes for soil samples, see 3.4.1), strength index test, and swelling.
sections.body: Terms common to all Eurocodes are defined in EN 1990; terms common to Eurocode 7 are defined in EN 1997-1:2004, 1.5.2. Specific definitions used in EN 1997-2 include: derived value - value of a geotechnical parameter obtained from test results by theory, correlation or empiricism; disturbed sample - sample where the soil structure, water content and/or constituents have been changed during sampling; measured value - value that is measured in a test; natural specimen - specimen made from the available (disturbed, undisturbed, remoulded) sample; quality class - classification by which the quality of a soil sample is assessed in the laboratory (soil samples are classified in five quality classes, see 3.4.1); remoulded sample - sample of which the soil or rock structure is fully disturbed; remoulded specimen - fully disturbed specimen at natural water content; re-compacted specimen - specimen forced into a mould with a rammer or under desired static stress state; reconstituted specimen - specimen prepared in the laboratory (for fine soils, prepared as a slurry at or above the liquid limit and then consolidated; for coarse soils, poured or pluviated and compacted or consolidated); re-consolidated specimen - specimen compressed in a mould or cell under static pressure while allowing drainage; sample - portion of soil or rock recovered from the ground by sampling techniques; specimen - part of a soil or rock sample used for a laboratory test; strength index test - test yielding an indication of shear strength without necessarily giving a representative value; swelling - expansion due to reduction of effective stress from either reduction of total stress or absorption of water at constant total stress (includes the reverse of compression and consolidation); undisturbed sample - sample where no change in soil characteristics of practical significance has occurred.
key_points: Derived value = geotechnical parameter obtained from test results by theory, correlation, or empiricism (distinct from a directly measured value)
Soil samples for laboratory testing are classified into five quality classes (see Table 3.1)
Reconstituted specimen: fine soils prepared as slurry above the liquid limit then consolidated; coarse soils poured/pluviated and compacted
Strength index test: yields an indication (not necessarily a representative value) of shear strength, results subject to uncertainty
Swelling includes the reverse of both compression and consolidation
sections.applicability: Provides the controlled vocabulary used throughout EN 1997-2 for sample/specimen types and derived-value terminology.

sections.title: Test results and derived values
sections.summary: Establishes the general framework: test results and derived values (from theory, correlation, or empiricism) feed the selection of characteristic geotechnical parameter values (EN 1997-1), which are then reduced by partial factors to design values. Annex A lists test-result types by test standard; correlation examples are given in the annexes to Section 4.
sections.body: Test results and derived values form the basis for the selection of characteristic values of ground properties used for geotechnical structure design, per EN 1997-1:2004, 2.4.3. Geotechnical design proceeds through successive phases (Figure 1.1): site investigation and testing (covered by this standard), determination of characteristic values, and design verification calculations (both covered by EN 1997-1). Test results can be experimental curves or values of geotechnical parameters; Annex A gives a list of test results to serve as a reference to test standards. Derived values of geotechnical parameters and/or coefficients are obtained from test results by theory, correlation, or empiricism. The example correlations used to determine derived values, given in the annexes to Section 4 of this standard (Annexes D-K), are obtained from the literature; they may correlate a geotechnical parameter or coefficient with a test result (such as qc from a CPT), or connect a parameter to a test result through theoretical considerations (e.g. deriving phi' from pressuremeter results or the plasticity index). In certain cases, derivation of geotechnical parameters by correlation is made after the test results have been corrected or transformed into conservative estimates, rather than before determination of the characteristic value.
key_points: Geotechnical design: site investigation/testing (EN 1997-2) -> characteristic values -> design values via partial factors (EN 1997-1)
Test results = experimental curves or parameter values; Annex A cross-references test standards to their result types
Derived values = parameters obtained from test results by theory, correlation, or empiricism
Annexes D-K (to Section 4) give example literature correlations used to establish derived values
Correlation-derived parameters may be based on raw test results or on already-corrected/conservative-transformed results
figures: Figure 1.1: General framework for the selection of derived values of geotechnical properties
Figure 1.2: General architecture of the CEN standards linked with EN 1997
sections.applicability: Defines how raw test results become derived parameter values and where that fits in the overall geotechnical design process shared with EN 1997-1.

sections.title: The link between EN 1997-1 and EN 1997-2
sections.summary: EN 1997-1 covers design rules (characteristic/design values, general site-investigation framework, structure design rules); EN 1997-2 covers detailed site investigation rules, general test specifications, derivation of ground properties, and worked calculation examples from field/lab tests; both rely on CEN/TC 341 test standards and CEN/TC 288 execution standards.
sections.body: Figure 1.2 presents the general architecture of CEN standards related to geotechnical engineering and directly linked to EN 1997. EN 1997-1 covers the design part: general framework for geotechnical design, definition of ground parameters, characteristic and design values, general rules for site investigation, rules for the design of the main types of geotechnical structures, and some assumptions on execution procedures. EN 1997-2 (this standard) gives rules for ground investigations and obtaining geotechnical parameter/coefficient values used to determine characteristic values as specified in EN 1997-1: detailed rules for site investigations, general test specifications, derivation of ground properties and the geotechnical model of the site, and examples of calculation methods based on field and laboratory tests. Implementation of EN 1997 also needs information from other standards, particularly the CEN/TC 341 test standards (drilling/sampling/groundwater measurement methods; laboratory and field tests on soils and rocks; tests on structures or parts of structures; identification and classification of soils and rocks) and the CEN/TC 288 execution-of-geotechnical-works standards.
key_points: EN 1997-1: design rules, characteristic/design values, general site-investigation framework, structural design rules
EN 1997-2: detailed site-investigation rules, test specifications, derivation of ground properties, worked calculation examples
CEN/TC 341 prepares the underlying test standards (drilling/sampling, lab/field tests, structure tests, soil/rock classification)
CEN/TC 288 prepares the execution-of-geotechnical-works standards
figures: Figure 1.2: General architecture of the CEN standards linked with EN 1997
sections.applicability: Clarifies the division of labor between EN 1997-1 (design) and EN 1997-2 (investigation/testing) and their shared supporting standards.

sections.title: Symbols and units
sections.summary: Defines the Latin/Greek symbols (e.g. E' drained modulus, EM/PLM Menard pressuremeter modulus/limit pressure, Nk/Nkt CPT cone factors, N60/(N1)60 corrected SPT blow counts, mu the FVT correction factor, alpha the CPT-Eoed correlation factor) and abbreviations (CPT, CPTU, DMT, DP variants, FVT, PMT variants, PLT, SPT, WST) used throughout the standard; recommended SI units are kN, kNm, kPa, m/s.
sections.body: For the purposes of EN 1997-2, a comprehensive symbol list applies (notation based on ISO 3898:1997), including: Cc (compression index), c' (cohesion intercept, effective stress), Cfv (undrained shear strength from FVT), cu (undrained shear strength), Cs (swelling index), Cv (coefficient of consolidation), D10/D15/D30/D60/D85 (particle sizes), E (Young's modulus), E' (drained/long-term Young's modulus), EFDT (flexible dilatometer modulus), EM (Menard pressuremeter modulus), Eoed (oedometer modulus), EpLT (plate loading test modulus), Er (energy ratio = Emeas/Etheor), Eu (undrained Young's modulus), IA (activity index), Ic (consistency index), ID (density index), IDMT (DMT material index), KDMT (DMT horizontal stress index), k (coefficient of permeability), IL (liquidity index), Ip (plasticity index), ks (coefficient of sub-grade reaction), N (SPT blow count per 300 mm), Nk/Nkt (CPT/CPTU cone factors, Eq 4.1/4.2), N10L/N10M/N10H/N10SA/N10SB/N20SA/N20SB (dynamic probing blow counts), N60/(N1)60 (energy- and overburden-corrected SPT blow counts), PLM (Menard limit pressure), qc (cone penetration resistance), qt (qc corrected for pore pressure), qu (unconfined compressive strength), wopt (optimum water content); Greek letters: alpha (Eoed-qc correlation factor, Eq 4.3), phi/phi' (angle of shearing resistance), mu (FVT correction factor, Eq 4.4), rho_d;max (max dry density), sigma_c (unconfined compression strength of rock, or tensile strength context-dependent), sigma'p (pre-consolidation pressure/yield stress), sigma_v0 (initial vertical total stress), sigma'v0 (initial vertical effective stress), v (Poisson's ratio). Test-type abbreviations: CPT/CPTM/CPTU, DMT, DP/DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH-A/DPSH-B, FDP (full displacement pressuremeter), FDT (flexible dilatometer test), FVT, MPM (Menard pressuremeter), PBP (pre-bored pressuremeter), PLT, PMT, RDT (rock dilatometer test), SBP (self-boring pressuremeter), SDT (soil dilatometer test), SPT, WST. Recommended SI units: force kN, moment kNm, mass density and weight density, stress/pressure/strength/stiffness kPa, coefficient of permeability m/s, coefficient of consolidation (area/time).
key_points: Nk and Nkt: CPT and CPTU cone factors used in Eq 4.1/4.2 for cu
alpha: correlation factor between Eoed and qc (Eq 4.3); mu: FVT correction factor (Eq 4.4)
IDMT and KDMT: DMT material index and horizontal stress index, used throughout Annex J and Eq 4.5
N60 / (N1)60: SPT blow count corrected for energy losses, and additionally normalized for effective overburden stress
Test abbreviations: CPT/CPTU/CPTM, DMT, DP family (DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH-A/DPSH-B), FVT, PMT family (MPM/PBP/SBP/FDP), FDT/RDT/SDT, PLT, SPT, WST
Recommended SI units: kN (force), kNm (moment), kPa (stress/pressure/strength/stiffness), m/s (permeability)
sections.applicability: Reference symbol table for interpreting every equation and correlation elsewhere in the standard.
